questions.stem: How are inhaled anaesthetic agents mainly eliminated from the body?
Does recovery from an inhaled agent simply reverse its induction?
options: No, they are not mirror images
Yes, but only with nitrous oxide

questions.stem: Why do highly fat-soluble agents slow recovery after long anaesthetics in obese patients?
options: They are cleared rapidly by the lungs
They build up in fat stores
They are inactivated by plasma enzymes

questions.stem: Of an inhaled anaesthetic dose, only a small ____ is metabolised.
At steady state, how are alveolar, arterial and brain partial pressures related?
Why is alveolar partial pressure useful to monitor during inhalational anaesthesia?
questions.answer: It is an indirect measure of brain partial pressure

questions.stem: How long can alveolar and brain agent levels take to reach steady state?
What sets how fast alveolar and brain partial pressures approach equilibrium?
Why does a high inspired concentration speed inhalational induction?
options: It creates a larger alveolar-blood gradient
It slows the rise in arterial level

questions.stem: On emergence with zero inspired concentration, where is the agent driven from the blood?
Why does more alveolar ventilation speed inhalational onset?
What does high minute ventilation do to inhalational induction and emergence?
For speeding induction, which agents does alveolar ventilation affect most?
options: Insoluble agents such as nitrous oxide
Soluble agents such as diethyl ether

questions.stem: Why does a large functional residual capacity slow inhalational onset?
What does nitrous oxide do to a companion inhaled agent, the second gas?
The blood–gas partition coefficient is also called the ____ solubility coefficient.
What determines the anaesthetic effect of an inhaled agent?
options: Partial pressure in blood and brain
Volume of agent in the cylinder

questions.stem: Why is induction slower with highly soluble inhaled agents?
questions.answer: A larger blood reservoir must fill first

questions.stem: A large blood reservoir for soluble agents slows induction and also slows ____.
At equilibrium, the blood–gas partition coefficient is the ratio of what?
options: Agent amount in blood to gas
Agent amount in gas to blood

questions.stem: What does a lower blood–gas partition coefficient do to induction and washout speed?
With other factors equal, isoflurane induction and emergence are ____ than desflurane.
Why does low cardiac output speed inhalational onset?
options: More uptake, so alveolar level rises slower
Less uptake, so alveolar level rises faster
Greater minute ventilation slows alveolar rise
Higher blood flow dilutes the agent

questions.stem: Why does high cardiac output slow the alveolar rise of an inhaled agent?
questions.answer: It keeps the alveolar-blood gradient high

questions.stem: How much does cardiac output affect modern, fairly insoluble inhaled agents?
options: Exactly as much as soluble agents

questions.stem: How is the brain–blood partition coefficient defined?
options: Brain-to-blood agent concentration ratio at equal partial pressures
Blood-to-brain agent concentration ratio at equal volumes

questions.stem: The brain–blood coefficient sets how fast the brain ____.
What does a lower brain–blood coefficient do to induction and emergence?
Which decrement time matters if waking follows a 50% fall in concentration?
As anaesthesia lengthens, what happens to decrement time differences between agents?
Which decrement time is almost identical across inhaled agents?
What mainly determines the first phase of inhaled agent elimination?
